haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes from creation (expires_at). If not claimed in time, the Inventory sweeper, on an unset interval, changes HELD to EXPIRED and the stock is available again. The order's status does not change.
haiku-low.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge; Order sends the charge only after reserve succeeds. If one line is short, nothing is held or charged. Order is REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, and Cart shows the short items and stays unchanged.
haiku-low.q3: The charge is keyed by order id. Payment finds an existing charge instead of creating another, and retries reuse the same key. The provider must honour the key, which is open question 7.
haiku-low.q4: Order's claim is refused, so it becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK with refund REQUESTED. Payment refunds the full amount. After RefundSucceeded, the order becomes CANCELLED_REFUNDED, OrderFailed with OUT_OF_STOCK is published, and the customer is emailed.
haiku-low.q5: Cart is emptied only on OrderConfirmed, if it is AWAITING_PAYMENT and the attempt and cart ids match. On checkout failure the cart is unchanged: it returns to OPEN with lines kept, so the customer can retry.
haiku-low.q6: Order's steps are run by the Place order handler and Order's recovery worker. Progress is stored in the order record: status, charge acknowledged, refund state, pending releases and outbox.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment (or a status query after 30 minutes). Payment writes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined to its outbox and publishes it to the broker. Order consumes it and finishes the order.
haiku-low.q8: Payment records the provider event id in the same transaction as the state change, so duplicates change nothing. Order treats a repeated request for its current status as a no-op, and consumers handle at-least-once redelivery.
haiku-low.q9: Order receives PaymentDeclined, moves to PAYMENT_DECLINED and writes a pending release row. A worker retries the release keyed by order id until Inventory sets the HELD reservation to RELEASED.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory's claim is refused if the hold has expired or is not HELD. Order then goes to CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and refunds. The design does not re-reserve stock for a late success (open question 9).
haiku-low.q11: Payment keeps the refund open, retries the provider call with the same key and backoff, and alerts operations; it is never dropped. The refund is tracked in Payment keyed by refund: plus order id.
haiku-low.q12: OrderConfirmed clears the cart, applied by the Cart service (step C5). It applies only if the cart is AWAITING_PAYMENT and the attempt and cart ids match.

sonnet.q1: Held 10 minutes (expires_at = created + 10 min). If not claimed, the sweeper (runs on a timer, interval not set) changes the HELD row to EXPIRED, making stock available again; an expired hold cannot be claimed even before the sweeper runs. Order status does not change on expiry.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge (reserve, then charge; Order commits AWAITING_PAYMENT after reserve and before sending the charge). If any line is short, Inventory writes a SHORT row with the short items, holds nothing for any line, Order goes REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK and nothing is charged; cart unchanged with short items shown.
sonnet.q3: The charge is keyed by order id. Payment finds an existing charge with that key and does not create another, replying CHARGE_RECORDED. Payment also retries the provider call with the same idempotency key (the provider must honour it, open question 7), so a retry never causes a second charge.
sonnet.q4: Inventory refuses the claim; Order moves to CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK with refund state REQUESTED in one transaction. The customer is refunded in full via Payment (refund keyed refund:+order id). After RefundSucceeded, the order becomes CANCELLED_REFUNDED, OrderFailed (reason OUT_OF_STOCK) is published and the customer is emailed.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only on a CONFIRMED outcome (OrderConfirmed event or FINAL CONFIRMED reply), applied by Cart. On any failure (short stock, checkout failed, declined, out-of-stock refund) Cart goes back to OPEN with lines unchanged, shows the message, and the customer can retry.
sonnet.q6: Order drives the steps (the Place order handler starts them, and they keep running inside Order after an IN_PROGRESS reply; the Order recovery worker resumes them after a restart). The record of progress is Order's own stored state: the order status, reserve attempt count, charge acknowledged flag, refund state, pending releases and outbox, in the order record unique on attempt id.
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment (or Payment queries status after 30 min, or the immediate reply is final). Payment records the result and writes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined to its outbox in the same transaction; the relay publishes it to the broker, and Order consumes it.
sonnet.q8: Several layers. Payment records the provider event id in the same transaction as the state change, so duplicate webhooks change nothing. A final charge does not change again. Order treats a message asking for the status the order already has as a no-op, and never claims again after a refusal or starts a second refund. Claim and other calls are keyed/idempotent. Cart ignores duplicate events since its status is already OPEN.
sonnet.q9: Order moves to PAYMENT_DECLINED on PaymentDeclined and writes a pending-release row in the same transaction. A worker retries the release to Inventory with the same key until acknowledged; Inventory sets a HELD reservation to RELEASED. The sweeper is the backstop.
sonnet.q10: The decision is made by Inventory's claim: it succeeds only if the reservation is HELD and now is before expires_at (or already CLAIMED). If accepted, the order is CONFIRMED; if refused (expired/released), Order cancels as CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and refunds. The design does not re-reserve stock (open question 9).
sonnet.q11: Payment keeps the refund open, retries the provider call with the same key and backoff, alerts operations, and never drops it. Order stays CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and learns only through RefundSucceeded; Cart stays payment pending. Pending refund is tracked in Payment (refunds keyed by refund:+order id) and in Order (refund state REQUESTED/ACKNOWLEDGED/SUCCEEDED).
sonnet.q12: Cart does it, when it applies a final CONFIRMED outcome (an OrderConfirmed event, or a FINAL CONFIRMED reply to a Place order retry). Only if cart status is AWAITING_PAYMENT, attempt id matches (and cart id for events); it sets status OPEN and empties the cart in the same step. Order publishes OrderConfirmed.
